question: What is the primary purpose of a multidisciplinary team in community health?

options.A: To reduce the number of working hours for individual nurses
options.B: To eliminate the need for community health extension workers
options.C: To transfer all administrative duties away from the clinic
options.D: To combine diverse professional skills for comprehensive patient care

explanation: Different health workers bring specialized knowledge together to address all aspects of a patient's well-being. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T24#GNS225_U2_T24_h1)

question: How does team collaboration directly benefit a rural health clinic with limited supplies?

options.A: By replacing physical medications with community health lectures
options.B: By preventing duplication of services and optimizing resource use
options.C: By increasing the budget allocated from the federal government
options.D: By removing the requirement for patient home visitation logs

explanation: Pooling expertise and materials ensures that scarce healthcare items are distributed efficiently without waste. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T24#GNS225_U2_T24_h1)

question: Mutual respect within a healthcare team primarily acknowledges what fact?

options.A: No single profession holds all answers to health challenges
options.B: Community volunteers possess formal medical degrees
options.C: Doctors must make every final clinical decision alone
options.D: Nurses hold the exact same training as environmental officers

explanation: Recognizing the limits of one's own profession encourages genuine reliance on other team specialists. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T24#GNS225_U2_T24_h2)

question: Shared decision-making in community care specifically involves which action?

options.A: Patients and team members contributing to setting care goals
options.B: The senior nursing officer dictating the treatment plan entirely
options.C: Voting on medical diagnoses during a general staff meeting
options.D: Allowing community leaders to prescribe basic malaria drugs

explanation: True collaboration includes the patient and all relevant workers in determining the best path forward. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T24#GNS225_U2_T24_h2)

question: Which team member is primarily responsible for inspecting community sanitation and water sources?
explanation: Sanitation, vector control, and safe water inspection fall directly under environmental health duties. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T24#GNS225_U2_T24_h3)

question: A patient with severe financial distress and chronic illness needs assistance finding welfare support. Who is best suited to help?
explanation: Social workers specialize in evaluating economic needs and connecting vulnerable clients to welfare resources. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T24#GNS225_U2_T24_h3)

question: What does the acronym ISBAR stand for in clinical communication?
explanation: ISBAR is a structured tool used by health professionals to organize clinical handovers effectively. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T24#GNS225_U2_T24_h4)

question: Why is structured communication essential during patient transfers from a village clinic to a general hospital?

options.A: It eliminates the need for written patient consent
options.B: It prevents vital clinical details from getting lost
options.C: It speeds up the process by skipping physical examinations
options.D: It reduces the financial cost of the ambulance fuel

explanation: Standardized sharing ensures receiving clinicians understand the exact patient history and current status. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T24#GNS225_U2_T24_h4)

question: A nutritionist is added to a diabetic patient's care plan primarily to achieve what goal?

options.A: Administer daily insulin injections during morning home visits
options.B: Provide financial grants for purchasing specialized diabetic shoes
options.C: Evaluate local food availability and suggest appropriate dietary options
options.D: Diagnose underlying pancreatic pathology causing high blood sugar

explanation: Nutritionists adapt dietary advice to what is practically accessible and affordable within the local environment. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T24#GNS225_U2_T24_h5)

question: A patient cannot afford prescribed medications during home care implementation. What is the best team action?

options.A: Instruct the family to take out a high-interest commercial loan
options.B: Discharge the patient from community follow-up immediately
options.C: Reconvene to adjust the care plan and find alternative solutions
options.D: Stop documenting the medication requirement in the clinical notes

explanation: When barriers arise, flexible teams collaborate to modify the plan rather than letting care fail. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T24#GNS225_U2_T24_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common barrier to effective multidisciplinary teamwork?

options.D: Unclear role definitions among team staff

explanation: An open and transparent hierarchy helps prevent teamwork breakdowns, whereas rigid and closed hierarchies create barriers. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T24#GNS225_U2_T24_h6)

question: How can a team overcome the barrier of professional hierarchy in a health clinic?

options.A: Requiring all team members to hold the exact same academic degree
options.B: Allowing senior physicians to make every decision without discussion
options.C: Banning doctors from attending routine nursing handover sessions
options.D: Fostering an open culture where junior staff feel safe speaking up

explanation: Encouraging all voices ensures critical patient observations are shared regardless of professional rank. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T24#GNS225_U2_T24_h6)

question: What is the main purpose of using the Plan-Do-Study-Act (PDSA) model in team practice?

options.A: To replace clinical guidelines with community opinions
options.B: To calculate monthly staff salaries and hazard allowances
options.C: To punish staff members who make documentation errors
options.D: To test small changes and refine collaborative workflows

explanation: PDSA cycles provide a structured framework for continuous quality improvement in healthcare delivery. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T24#GNS225_U2_T24_h7)

question: Why should a community health team conduct debriefing sessions after handling a critical incident?

options.A: To assign formal blame to the most junior nurse on duty
options.B: To complete mandatory legal paperwork for the police department
options.C: To extend the working hours of the primary health center staff
options.D: To identify coordination successes and breakdowns for future improvement

explanation: Reviewing critical events helps teams learn from experience and improve future collaborative responses. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T24#GNS225_U2_T24_h7)
